Article Title: India's roads kill quietly while crashes in the sky make headlines
Article Text:
Uttarakhand Helicopter Crash

Roads: A death every three minutes

India's deadly roads: Over 500 lives lost every day

Railways: Fewer train crashes, thousands still die on tracks

Aviation: 60 deaths in smaller aircraft since 2021

22 lives lost: Small aircraft crashes hit 6-year high

Uttarakhand's helicopter toll

The daily toll that draws less attention

Six people were killed on Friday when a Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter flying from Badrinath to Dehradun crashed near Chai village in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district. The operator's fleet has been grounded and the cause is under investigation.The crash takes this year's toll in smaller civilian aircraft accidents to 22 deaths in six fatal accidents, the highest annual figure in a TOI compilation covering January 2021 to October 2026.Yet these deaths are a small part of India's transport toll. Roads kill more than 500 people every day. Major train accidents have fallen sharply, but thousands still die on railway tracks and premises. Scattered across individual incidents, many of these deaths receive little attention compared with major disasters.Road accidents killed 1,83,434 people in 2025, up 3.5% from 1,77,175 in 2024, according to provisional figures the road transport ministry gave Parliament. There were 5,13,474 crashes, about 1,407 a day. On average, 503 people died every day, nearly 21 every hour. The figures come from the government's Electronic Detailed Accident Report (e-DAR) portal as of July 27, 2026.Road deaths have risen every year since 2021, when 1,53,972 people were killed.The toll is up about 19% in four years. Crashes have also grown deadlier over the long term. Accident severity, measured as deaths per 100 reported accidents, rose from 21.6 in 2005 to 36.3 in 2024. Provisional figures indicate a slight dip to 35.7 in 2025.National highways make up only 2.1% of India's road network but accounted for 36.6% of road deaths in 2024, or 64,772 lives. Provisional figures show that highway deaths fell 4.1% to 62,122 in 2025, even as overall road fatalities rose.Uttar Pradesh recorded the most deaths in 2025 (27,547) and Tamil Nadu the most accidents (71,195). India has committed to halving road traffic deaths and injuries by 2030. The government has also announced a new rating system for national highways that will assess road conditions, safety and user experience.Consequential train accidents, which include collisions, derailments, fires and level-crossing accidents, fell from 135 in 2014-15 to 31 in 2024-25 and 16 in 2025-26, an 88% drop over 11 years. They killed 17 people in 2025-26, against 18 the year before.A single disaster can still be devastating. The Balasore triple-train collision in Odisha on June 2, 2023, killed 296 people and injured more than 1,200. Investigators identified signalling and interlocking lapses linked to the crash.The overall trend, however, is downward. Accidents per million train-kilometres fell from 0.11 to 0.01 between 2014-15 and 2025-26. The government credits improvements in signalling, track maintenance, rolling stock and safety technology, including the Kavach automatic train protection system. Spending and budget allocations for railway safety rose from Rs 39,200 crore in 2013-14 to Rs 1,17,693 crore in 2025-26.But far more people die around the railway network than in major train accidents.The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) recorded 22,413 deaths on railway tracks and premises in 2024, and another 1,888 at railway crossings, a total of 24,301. Of the 22,413 deaths on tracks and premises, 17,029 involved people falling from trains or being struck on the tracks. Maharashtra recorded the most deaths on railway tracks and premises in 2024 (3,587), followed by Uttar Pradesh (3,538). Separately, Government Railway Police data recorded 2,468 deaths on Mumbai's suburban railway network that year, down from 2,590 in 2023.Air crashes kill far fewer people overall. A July 2025 parliamentary reply counted 18 accidents involving Indian-registered scheduled aircraft since 2015. But a single disaster can claim hundreds. The Air India AI171 crash in Ahmedabad on June 12, 2025, killed 260 people: 241 aboard and 19 on the ground.Smaller aircraft are counted separately. A TOI review of accident reports, government records and news reports finds at least 60 deaths in 19 fatal accidents involving smaller civilian aircraft between January 2021 and October 2026. These involved helicopters, chartered aircraft, training planes, air ambulances and small regional passenger aircraft. The compilation excludes military aircraft and large commercial airliners.The annual toll was one death in 2021, 14 in 2022, four in 2023, five in 2024, 14 in 2025 and 22 so far in 2026. Helicopters accounted for 37 of the 60 deaths and fixed-wing aircraft for 23.This year's accidents span different kinds of operations. A passenger died after an IndiaOne Air aircraft made a forced landing near Rourkela in January. Later that month, a Learjet crash at Baramati killed five, including Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar In February, seven died in an air-ambulance crash in Jharkhand's Chatra district, and another passenger died after a Pawan Hans helicopter crash near Mayabunder in the Andamans. A training-aircraft crash near Kanpur killed two in August, followed by Friday's six deaths near Joshimath.The Baramati, Chatra and Joshimath crashes alone accounted for 18 of this year's 22 deaths.Uttarakhand accounted for 21 of the 30 helicopter-accident deaths in India during the preceding five years, or 70%, according to a July 2025 government reply in the Rajya Sabha. In TOI's compilation, 27 of the 60 deaths are linked to pilgrimage helicopter flights.The AAIB's final report on the June 2025 Gaurikund crash in Uttarakhand, which killed seven, cited rapidly descending clouds, delayed flight-path decisions and limited experience in the Kedarnath valley. It recommended 50 hours of supervised hill flying before pilots undertake single-pilot operations in the valley for the first time.Nationally, the helicopter accident rate rose from 0.33 per 10,000 flying hours in 2024 to 0.53 in 2025, although four accidents in 2025 are too few to establish a sustained deterioration in safety.Investigators also found visibility below the minimum for visual flying and faded runway markings at Baramati, and inadequate flight-data-monitoring records at the Kanpur flying school.These findings point to operational weaknesses, but they do not establish that smaller aircraft are inherently more dangerous than commercial airliners.At the 2025 average, India's roads claimed roughly as many lives every 12½ hours as the 260 people killed in the AI171 crash. A single average day's road toll was nearly 30 times the number killed in consequential train accidents in all of 2025-26. Air and train disasters bring immediate investigations and extensive coverage. Road deaths, spread across lakhs of crashes, rarely receive the same sustained attention.The railways show that sustained investment and safety measures can coincide with a sharp fall in major operational accidents. The challenge is to bring similar attention to road safety, deaths around railway tracks and the oversight of smaller aircraft, areas where prevention rarely draws the attention that disasters do.
Article Summary: Road accidents killed 1,83,434 people in 2025, up 3.5% from 1,77,175 in 2024. Road deaths have risen every year since 2021, when 1,53,972 people were killed. On average, 503 people died every day, nearly 21 every hour.

Article Title: Discontent in Abdullahs' NC: Minister says party stands strong, dismisses impact of MP's exit
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing resentment within the National Conference camp over the recent cabinet expansion, Jammu and Kashmir minister Javed Rana on Saturday said the party remained strong, with no resentment among its ranks, and dismissed speculation that Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi's planned exit would affect the party."If Agha Sahab decides to part ways, he will do so alone. If he leaves, he leaves by himself... Why would it affect the party?" Rana said, responding to questions about Ruhullah's decision to resign from the party and his Lok Sabha seat on November 3.Rana said the government was robust under chief minister Omar Abdullah and the party organisation, under the leadership of Farooq Abdullah, stood firm."There is no resentment (in JKNC). The Jammu & Kashmir National Conference is strong, the government under the leadership of the chief minister is robust, and the organisation, under the leadership of Dr Farooq Sahab, stands firm, as solid as a rock," he said.Rana also said the reported discontent within the party was due to the limited number of ministerial positions, adding that several legislators aspired to join the cabinet but the available slots were restricted.He also expressed hope that statehood would be restored soon and more ministers would be appointed."There are celebrations taking place across J&K regarding the cabinet expansion. I do not see any signs of discontent anywhere.Was any statement issued on their behalf? I do not believe there is any substantive evidence to support such claims," he said."There is no real resentment; it is simply a case of 'every MLA wishing to become a minister', but the available slots are very limited. Insha'Allah, statehood will be restored soon, and insha'Allah, ministers will be appointed," he added.Cracks widened in the National Conference following the J&K cabinet expansion and a meeting of party legislators. The developments have also coincided with Ruhullah's announcement that he would quit the party and resign from his parliamentary seat on November 3.Meanwhile, according to sources, over a dozen party legislators met on Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone, who represents the Lolab constituency, with several others joining the meeting online.They decided to seek the resignation of the entire council of ministers and demand that a new cabinet be formed through consensus, based on merit and in keeping with democratic principles, sources said. They also decided to seek the resignation of chief minister's advisor Nasir Ahmad Wani.JKNC Kashmir president Showkat Ahmad Mir acknowledged that some party members had expressed concerns following the cabinet expansion, describing such differences as part of the party's internal democratic process."Following the expansion of the cabinet, some individuals expressed their concerns, which they are entitled to do as part of the internal democracy of the party. Regarding the meeting that took place yesterday, some MLAs with whom I am in touch mentioned receiving a phone call about a 'Darbar Move', where they discussed various pros and cons. Once they left, the situation was blown out of proportion with claims of 27 members involved, largely fuelled by the BJP, which is keen on spreading such rumours," Mir told news agency ANI."The BJP promised the people of Jammu that they would restore statehood and secured votes on that basis; today, the people of Jammu are rebuking them severely," he added.
Article Summary: Cracks widened in the National Conference following the J&K cabinet expansion and a meeting of party legislators. Jammu and Kashmir minister Javed Rana said the party remained strong, with no resentment among its ranks. He dismissed speculation that Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi's planned exit would affect the party.

Article Title: 'Public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar: INDIA bloc event to begin shortly at Kharge's residence - top developments
Article Text:
AISA chief Neha Bora arrives at Kharge's residence

CEC has 'disqualified' himself as an 'impartial umpire': Shashi Tharoor on 'public impeachment'

NEW DELHI: The Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc will shortly hold its "public impeachment"programme against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, a day after postponing the exercise by 24 hours due to rain in Delhi.The symbolic exercise will be held at 10, Rajaji Marg, the residence of Congress president and Rajya Sabha leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge . Kumar has been facing allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Separately, The Indian Express reported last month that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those concerning the SIR, adding to the scrutiny of Kumar.The "impeachment" exercise is being held a day ahead of the INDIA bloc's "Delhi Chalo" rally at Ramlila Maidan, where the opposition will seek Kumar's resignation.Student activist Neha Bora, president of All India Students' Association, arrives for the programme."I have come for the public impeachment. This impeachment—something people across India have been demanding for a long time—is taking place here today.If those currently in power in Parliament were truly representing the interests of the people, then what is happening here today would instead be taking place inside our Parliament," she told reporters.According to Congress MP Shashi Tharoor, the "public impeachment" programme is being held to reinforce that CEC Kumar has "disqualified himself as an impartial umpire" of the electoral process."I understand that the Congress party and the other opposition parties' notices of impeachment have not been admitted by the presiding officers of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha. This is why we have no choice but to conduct the impeachment here," Tharoor told reporters outside the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.After being successively unsuccessful in creating anarchy in India, the Congress party, just in order to give solace to the sentiment of their maverick prince, Rahul Gandhi, is now creating a hallucination that he is there in the Parliament of his own choice by creating a mock parliament: BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi
Article Summary: Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc will shortly hold its "public impeachment"programme against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The symbolic exercise will be held at 10, Rajaji Marg, the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. Kumar has been facing allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Article Title: ‘If match umpire is biased, what is the point of playing?’ Sachin Pilot questions CEC’s neutrality
Article Text:
Pilot questions CEC's neutrality

Pilot questions CEC appointment process, immunity law

Congress plans public impeachment proceeding against CEC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Saturday questioned the neutrality of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that his conduct and the process governing his appointment and post-retirement immunity had raised concerns about the independence of the Election Commission.In an interview with news agency ANI, Pilot alleged that the CEC's actions had undermined public confidence in the electoral institution and called for accountability over the alleged deletion of names from electoral rolls.“If a match umpire is biased, what is the point of playing?”, Pilot said, questioning how voters could have faith in elections if the neutrality of the institution conducting them was under scrutiny.He referred to the alleged deletion of 13.3 crore names from electoral rolls, calling it a challenge to the fundamental right to vote. “13.3 crore people's names are known to be struck off the electoral rolls. It's a big challenge to what we believe is the most fundamental issue in our republic, which is the right to vote,” he said.Pilot claimed that the Congress had submitted documentary evidence of alleged wrongdoing by Gyanesh Kumar during his tenure as CEC.“There has been enough tangible data and documents proof given for the wrongdoings that Gyanesh Kumar has conducted through his term as Chief Election Commissioner,” he said.Pilot also questioned the legal provisions governing the appointment of the CEC and the immunity granted to the office-holder after demitting office.He said the earlier selection process involved the Prime Minister, the leader of opposition and the Chief Justice of India, and questioned the government's decision to change the composition of the selection panel.He also challenged the need for a law granting the CEC immunity after leaving office.“What was the need for the government to pass a new law which gives the chief election commissioner immunity for life? Now, he is the only person in the country, not the Prime Minister, not the chief ministers, not the Director of Intelligence or the Army Chief, but the only man who, after demitting office, will have immunity for life,” Pilot said.He alleged that the government had failed to address questions raised by the opposition in Parliament, arguing that the lack of answers had made it necessary to take the issue to the public.“As a political party, we are within our rights to raise this issue and demand answers,” he said.Pilot said the opposition was seeking to create awareness, particularly among young people, about the importance of independent electoral institutions. He maintained that institutions expected to function transparently should remain above political affiliations.He also said the legal challenge was already under way, with cases pending before the Supreme Court.“The fight is already going on at multiple levels. We also went to the Supreme Court. The cases are ongoing and are sub judice. The Election Commission has also given a clarification, which obviously you are not convinced about,” he said.The INDIA bloc has planned a public impeachment proceeding against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday. The event was postponed on Friday due to rain. The opposition bloc is also scheduled to hold a rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday against the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Congress leader Sachin Pilot questions neutrality of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Pilot questions CEC appointment process, immunity law.Congress plans public impeachment proceeding against CEC on Saturday. Opposition bloc also scheduled to hold a rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday.

Article Title: 'Historic day': PM Modi welcomes launch of Kashi-Delhi Vande Bharat sleeper train
Article Text:
Kashi-Delhi Vande Bharat sleeper train launched

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian Railways has launched the second Vande Bharat sleeper train, connecting Varanasi (Kashi) with New Delhi via Prayagraj and Kanpur Central, expanding the network of overnight semi-high-speed rail services. Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the launch, saying the service would save time and improve the travel experience for passengers.In a post on X, the Prime Minister described the development as a historic day for passengers travelling between Delhi and Kashi.“Today is a historic day for those traveling by rail between Delhi and Kashi. With the launch of the Kashi-Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper Train, not only will there be a saving of time, but their experience is also set to improve. Equipped with modern amenities and a state-of-the-art safety system, this is the country’s second Vande Bharat Sleeper Train,” he wrote.In another post, Modi highlighted the route's significance for pilgrims, tourists and business travellers, noting that the train would connect several important destinations across Uttar Pradesh.“The Vande Bharat Sleeper train running from Kashi to Prayagraj, via Kanpur Central, to Delhi will make travel convenient for millions of devotees, tourists, youth, and businesspeople,” he said.Emphasising the cultural and religious importance of the route, the Prime Minister added, “Whether it’s a darshan of Baba Vishwanath or a journey to the Sangam, this train will connect faith with opportunity and tradition with modernity. Heartfelt best wishes to everyone for this new rail service!”The new service will connect Varanasi, one of India's prominent spiritual and cultural destinations, with the national capital, while also improving connectivity for passengers travelling through Prayagraj and Kanpur.The 16-coach train will offer three accommodation classes: third AC, second AC and first AC and has a passenger capacity of 823.The service is expected to operate six days a week, covering approximately 760 km. Its introduction will extend the Vande Bharat sleeper network beyond the Howrah-Guwahati corridor, offering passengers another overnight travel option as Indian Railways expands its long-distance services.
Article Summary: Kashi-Delhi Vande Bharat sleeper train launched by Indian Railways. Train will connect Varanasi (Kashi) with New Delhi via Prayagraj and Kanpur Central. 16-coach train will offer three accommodation classes: third AC, second AC and first AC.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Saturday posed five questions to the Congress, a day before the opposition INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan to seek the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls."I challenge the Congress party to answer these basic questions," he posted on X.Rijiju first question was how the Congress managed to win just 44 seats in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, despite the polls being conducted by an Election Commission whose members were appointed under the then Congress-led UPA government.Pointing out that Kumar was not the CEC during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, having been appointed to the EC only ahead of the polls and elevated to the top post in 2025, the minister questioned how the Congress still lost, marking its third consecutive Lok Sabha election defeat.The Congress-led opposition has repeatedly accused Kumar of manipulating elections in favour of the BJP.Meanwhile, Rijiju further asked whether all sitting Congress chief ministers would resign and whether the party would apologise for forming governments between 2014 and 2026, if it had won elections despite alleged manipulation in the BJP's favour.His next questions focused on the SIR, with Rijiju asking whether illegal immigrants, deceased individuals and people who had relocated should be removed from electoral rolls, and whether the eight previous revision exercises were also "illegal."The current protests follow a report published by The Indian Express in September, which stated that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected at least 14 times to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those concerning the SIR.Responding to the report, the EC said that disagreements were common in multi-member institutions and that all decisions were ultimately taken unanimously.Decisions in the poll panel are taken either by consensus or by a 2-1 majority.

Article Title: 'Let's walk together': Rahul Gandhi invites people to march ahead of INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan
Article Text:
Delhi Police says no permission sought on INDIA bloc march to Ramlila Ground

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday invited people to join a march in the national capital on Sunday before reaching Ramlila Maidan, where the INDIA bloc is scheduled to hold a mega rally on November 1.However, Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI that no permission had been sought for the proposed march from Connaught Place.In a post on X, Rahul shared the route and schedule of the march, saying, "See you tomorrow, let's walk together."According to his post, the march will begin at the Minto Road junction near Connaught Place at noon on Sunday. Participants will proceed towards Ajmeri Gate before concluding at Ramlila Maidan.Responding to Rahul's announcement, Delhi Police sources told ANI that no application had been received seeking permission for a march from Connaught Place. They added that MPs and political leaders were free to travel in their private vehicles to the Constitution Club, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence or any other location of their choice.The sources also pointed out that Jantar Mantar, traditionally a designated venue for protests in the capital, has been de-notified as a protest site.They said Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which restricts assemblies and gatherings, is currently in force across the New Delhi area, including the vicinity of the Election Commission.Police said elaborate security arrangements would be made at Ramlila Maidan for Sunday's rally. Personnel from multiple Delhi Police districts, including the Central District, will be deployed along with paramilitary forces.Meanwhile, INDIA bloc leaders are scheduled to hold a public programme on the proposed impeachment of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar on Saturday at 3.30 pm at 10, Rajaji Marg, the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.The programme was postponed from Friday due to rain in the national capital. Announcing the decision, Gandhi said the leaders had agreed to reschedule it to avoid inconvenience to senior members.Speaking to reporters in Delhi on Friday, Rahul said, "By consensus, we have decided to postpone today's program (public impeachment programme against CEC) to tomorrow at the same time because of rain. We felt that it would be uncomfortable for seniors to sit in the rain, and we will hold the same program tomorrow."He also urged political parties, civil society members, journalists and other citizens to join the INDIA bloc's November 1 march to Ramlila Maidan."The day after, we have a march to Ramlila Maidan. All the opposition, everybody who wants to come: political, non-political, social, service people, civil society people, journalists. Both the programs are about the demolition of Indian democracy by Narendra Modi, by Amit Shah, by Gyanesh Kumar and his crew in the Election Commission," he said.Raebareli MP further alleged that Union home minister Amit Shah was trying to prevent people from travelling to Delhi to attend the rally."The home minister is trying his best to stop people from coming into Delhi, trying to ensure that our party members, common people who want to come from UP, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Telangana, Punjab, are being stopped. And they're trying their best," former Congress chief said.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi invited people to join a march in the national capital on Sunday. Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI that no permission had been sought for the proposed march from Connaught Place. Jantar Mantar, traditionally a designated venue for protests in the capital, has been de-notified as a protest site.

Article Title: IDBI sale sparks round 2 of Rahul-Sitharaman clash; FM blames Congress for bad loans

‘IDBI Bank was handed over to us in poor shape’

NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Friday defended the Centre's proposed sale of a controlling stake in IDBI Bank , hitting back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's criticism and accusing previous Congress-led governments of political interference and financial mismanagement.Responding to Rahul's opposition to the proposed sale of the bank to a subsidiary of Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings, Sitharaman said IDBI Bank was in a "distressed state when the NDA government took charge."In a post on X, the finance minister said previous Congress-led governments had treated banks and financial institutions as personal entities, pressuring employees to extend loans by bypassing lending norms."We all know how Congress has used Banks and financial institutions as personal entities and pressured bank employees to extend loans at their whim, bypassing prudent lending norms. Let me list a few instances. - In 1957, Haridas Mundra got money from LIC due to influence by the Congress leaders. - In 1976, Indira Gandhi's government removed SBI Chairman R.K. Talwar after he refused political pressure to relax lending conditions for a company linked to Sanjay Gandhi's circle.- Sanjay Gandhi pressured the Central Bank of India over loans to Maruti. - B. Janardhana Poojary, MoS Finance under Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi — pressured bank employees to issue loans in the 1980s. - Pawan Kumar Bansal, as a minister in the UPA, pressured Canara Bank to give loans to his family-linked businesses," she posted.Sitharaman also accused previous administrations of pushing IDBI bank to extend loans to large business groups with alleged links to Congress leaders. She named Videocon, Winsome, ABG Shipyard and Kingfisher, saying the loans later turned into non-performing assets (NPAs) and caused huge losses to the lender."The IDBI Bank was handed over to us in poor shape, as IDBI itself was forced to lend to large business groups with close connections to @INCIndia leaders such as Videocon, Winsome, ABG Shipyard, Kingfisher, etc. These turned into bad loans, causing huge losses for IDBI Bank, which we recognised," she added.The finance minister also cited a series of historical controversies to support her argument, including the 1957 Mundra scandal, the removal of State Bank of India chairman RK Talwar in 1976, alleged pressure over loans to Maruti and instances of political interference during the 1980s and the UPA era.Earlier on Friday, Rahul Gandhi extended support to IDBI Bank employees amid protests by bank unions and political parties against the Centre's decision to sell its stake in the lender.In a post on X, the Congress leader shared a letter addressed to the IDBI Bank family, criticising the government's move and contrasting it with the bank's establishment during the Congress regime."During Congress's time, IDBI was established—to build the nation's industry. During Modi's time, first the bidding was seen, then the price was set," he said."During Congress's time, banks were being created. During Modi's time, they are being sold. I stand with the employees of IDBI Bank," Rahul added.The Centre had said a day earlier that the proposed stake sale was part of a "strategic restructuring". It maintained that the process followed the provisions laid down in the request for proposal (RFP) and was undertaken after approval from a panel of secretaries and the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.The latest exchange marks the second round of sharp exchanges between Rahul and Sitharaman in three days. The two had first traded barbs on Wednesday over the boardroom battle at Bombay House, with Rahul accusing the government of allowing the Tata Group to be "criminally destroyed".Rahul had taken to X to criticise the developments at the conglomerate, saying, “Tata is being criminally destroyed, and no business leader dares say a word. How long will you stay silent? Until they own you? Indian business is not Modi and Shah’s plaything. You lack courage. We don’t. We will ensure justice for these crimes,”Within hours, Sitharaman hit back at the Congress leader, saying, “Being the LoP (leader of opposition in Lok Sabha) Rahul Gandhi, I suggest you refrain from politicising every issue. Also, casually labelling commercial and legal matters as criminal is unacceptable,”She also accused the Congress of harming the interests of Indian business.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman hits back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's criticism. She accuses previous Congress-led governments of political interference and financial mismanagement. Earlier on Friday, Rahul Gandhi extended support to IDBI Bank employees amid protests by bank unions.

NEW DELHI: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) in Delhi on Friday urged senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi to postpone the party's proposed mega rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, warning that it could disrupt business worth Rs 10,000-12,000 crore across 20 markets in the national capital.The trade body said the rally, proposed by leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, comes at a crucial time when markets are preparing for the Diwali shopping season.The trade body warned of severe economic losses during the peak festive shopping season.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) said the rally is expected to draw around 10 lakh people and 15,000 to 20,000 vehicles to central Delhi. It warned that the large gathering could lead to severe traffic congestion and affect the movement of goods and shoppers across the markets."We demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000–20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown," the CTI urged in its letter to Sonia Gandhi.The traders' body said the rally is planned at a crucial time for businesses, with Dhanteras falling on November 6 and Diwali on November 8. It said November 1 is expected to be one of the busiest days for transporting festive goods and for shoppers visiting the markets.CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said traders were worried about the possible impact on their livelihoods and stressed that the appeal was not against the rally."We are not opposing the rally; we are making a heartfelt plea to protect our livelihoods during the peak Diwali season," stated CTI Chairman Brijesh Goyal."These 20 markets are not merely marketplaces; they are the heartbeat of Delhi. They generate a daily turnover of 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees, and Dhanteras falls on November 6th. Traders are anxious: if a lockdown-like gridlock hits central Delhi on October 31st and November 1st, how will the goods for Dhanteras be transported in and out?" Goyal added."Dhanteras falls on November 6, and Diwali is on November 8; November 1 is the busiest day for preparations... If 1 million people and 15,000–20,000 vehicles arrive in Central Delhi on November 1, the daily business turnover of Rs 10,000–12,000 crore across 20 historic markets will come to a complete standstill," Goyal noted.In its letter, the CTI listed four major concerns. The first was the lack of parking space at Ramlila Maidan."Where will 15,000–20,000 vehicles be parked? Ramlila Maidan does not even have the capacity to park 200 large buses."The second concern was the possible disruption to 20 wholesale and retail markets within a 5-km radius of the venue. The CTI said these markets together record daily business worth Rs 10,000-12,000 crore.The markets include Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Connaught Place, Palika Bazar, Janpath, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Kashmiri Gate, Naya Bazar, Lajpat Rai Market, Chawri Bazar, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Ballimaran, Fatehpuri, Tilak Bazar, Karol Bagh, Jama Masjid, Nabi Karim, Gaffar Market, Ajmeri Gate-Paharganj and Daryaganj.The traders' body also warned that traffic restrictions could begin well before the rally. It said buses and other vehicles may start arriving at Delhi's borders, including Singhu, Tikri, Ghazipur and Badarpur, from the afternoon of October 31. Barricades could also be put up along Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg and JLN Marg by the evening.The CTI said transporters had already begun refusing to send vehicles to the markets from October 31.It also cited the traffic disruption during an earlier protest as a reason for concern."On October 10th, with only 5,000 to 7,000 people gathering at Jantar Mantar, central Delhi remained gridlocked for eight hours. Now, 1 million (10 lakh) people are expected to arrive."The CTI said the markets, some of which are up to 300 years old, supply goods to different parts of the country. It added that their operations depend on around 5,000 trucks and tempos arriving daily from 56 industrial areas, including Narela, Bawana, Okhla, Mayapuri, Mundka, Udyog Nagar and Mangolpuri.To avoid disruption during the festive season, the CTI has suggested two options. It has asked the organisers to postpone the rally until after November 10 or shift it to Burari Maidan if the November 1 date cannot be changed.The rally, called the 'Chalo Dilli Ramlila March', has been organised by the opposition INDIA bloc to protest against alleged vote tampering.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has said the march is not limited to any one political party and has appealed to people to join it."Chalo Dilli Ramlila March, it is a march to save democracy, to stop vote theft, to save the Constitution. This is not a march of any one political party; it is a march of the soul of India. All the people who are fed up with Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, and Gyanesh Kumar, all the people who want to save democracy, who want to protect the Constitution, you all come," Rahul Gandhi stated.The letter to Sonia Gandhi came after the trade body had also written to Rahul Gandhi, urging him to postpone the rally to avoid disrupting business during the festive season.With less than 48 hours left before the rally, traders are waiting for a response from the Congress leadership to their request.
Article Summary: Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) urges Sonia Gandhi to postpone Rahul Gandhi's rally. The rally is expected to draw around 10 lakh people and 15,000 to 20,000 vehicles to central Delhi. It warned that the large gathering could lead to severe traffic congestion and affect the movement of goods and shoppers.

Article Title: Firecracker ban: No point in passing orders without enforcement, says SC
Article Text:
SC said it is not inclined to completely ban firecrackers but warned authorities that orders are meaningless without ground-level enforcement

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it was not inclined to completely ban firecrackers, but there was no point in passing orders and directions every year unless authorities implement them on the ground.“It concerns every living being,” a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale observed while hearing a matter on the bursting of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR.Additional solicitor-general Aishwarya Bhati told the bench about the measures taken by Delhi govt and Commission for Air Quality Management to deal with air pollution.“There is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,” the bench observed, while stressing enforcement.While saying that it was not an adversarial matter, the bench observed that authorities have to take up the issue seriously and take action. “You have to really regulate it. Every year we are trying to balance it out but unless there is cooperation from everyone, it can’t be done,” it said.“We also understand the sentiments of the public. We are not inclined to completely ban, but don’t push us to take a very harsh stand,” the bench told Bhati.Bhati said a series of measures have been taken which would come into effect from Nov, including curbs on older vehicles, construction and demolition activity and staggered office timings in Delhi. “We are geared up to deal with the pollution season which unfortunately happens,” she said.Centre also told the bench that its internal consultation on the issue pertaining to the use of barium in firecrackers was going on. Bhati requested the bench to grant three weeks to complete the consultation.The top court was hearing two petitions, including a suo motu case concerning air pollution in NCR covering issues like firecrackers, stubble burning and solid waste management. The other plea relates to a ban on manufacturing firecrackers.During the hearing, an advocate, assisting the apex court as an amicus curiae in the suo motu case, said bursting firecrackers releases a huge amount of hazardous particulate matter (PM) which enters the human body and causes damage to lungs and other organs.She said during Dussehra last week, there was a spike in the Air Quality Index (AQI) in Delhi-NCR. Flagging the issue of enforcement, the amicus said there was no proper mechanism to assess whether the firecrackers which are being sold are actually green crackers.The bench had said that a middle ground would have to be found by specifying hours during which firecrackers could be used.
Article Summary: SC said it is not inclined to completely ban firecrackers but warned authorities that orders are meaningless without ground-level enforcement. “There is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,” the bench observed, while stressing enforcement.

Article Title: Surrender before December 1: Supreme Court cancels bail of expelled JD(U) leader Anant Singh in Dularchand Yadav murder case

Murder case and legal proceedings

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday cancelled the bail granted to expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Singh in the murder case of Dularchand Yadav and directed him to surrender before the authorities on or before December 1, 2026.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the Patna High Court had erred in granting Singh bail without adequately considering the nature of the offence and his criminal antecedents. The top court suspended the High Court's order and cancelled the relief granted to Singh.The verdict comes days after the ruling Janata Dal (United) expelled Singh and his wife, former MLA Neelam Devi, from the party for six years over alleged anti-party activities.Singh had openly defied the party leadership by campaigning for Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Kumar Singh instead of the JD(U)'s official nominee, Neeraj Kumar, in the Patna Graduates' constituency Legislative Council elections. He also reportedly made remarks against senior party leaders and questioned the functioning of the party leadership.Following the expulsion, the Bihar government stripped Neelam Devi of her position on the State-Level Programme Implementation Committee, withdrawing her minister of state rank and entitlement to an official bungalow.On October 26, the state government's Building Construction Department issued an eviction notice directing her to vacate her official residence at 1, Mall Road in Patna.The JD(U) has also approached Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh's disqualification under the anti-defection law. The petition was filed under the direction of party state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha.Dularchand Yadav, a regional strongman, was murdered on October 30, 2025, during a clash in Mokama Tal while campaigning for the Bihar Assembly elections was underway. Yadav was backing Jan Suraaj candidate Piyush Priyadarshi when his supporters allegedly clashed with Singh's convoy.According to the FIR registered at Ghoswari police station, Singh and his aides allegedly dragged Yadav out of his vehicle, shot him in the leg, assaulted him and ran over him with an SUV.Singh, however, claimed that the incident was part of a political conspiracy orchestrated by a rival politician. He alleged that Jan Suraaj supporters had attacked his convoy first.Bihar Police arrested Singh on November 1, 2025, and lodged him in Beur Central Jail. Despite being in custody, he contested and won the Mokama Assembly seat on a JD(U) ticket.The Patna high court granted him bail on March 19, 2026, following which he was released from prison. The bail order was subsequently challenged in the Supreme Court in October by Neeraj Kumar, the grandson of Dularchand Yadav.
Article Summary: Supreme Court cancels bail granted to expelled JD(U) MLA Anant Singh in the murder case of Dularchand Yadav. Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the Patna High Court had erred in granting Singh bail without adequately considering the nature of the offence and his criminal antecedents.

Article Title: Can amend privacy act, revoke law if needed: Government
Article Text:
​Centre open to amending DPDP Act rules or the law itself to address media concerns over its impact on press freedom, days after Supreme Court agreed to hear challenge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Centre Friday said it is open to changing the rules of Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and, if necessary, the law itself to eliminate the possibility of its application becoming an impediment for journalists and media houses.Senior officials at the ministry for electronics & information technology said that sections of the law, which have been flagged as violative of the constitutional provisions guaranteeing freedom of speech and expression, are applicable to data fiduciaries and they are not for journalists."This law is only on data fiduciaries-those who keep and control data. Journalists and media houses do not come under this category," When told about the worry among journalists that DPDP Act does not expressly exempt media houses, he said, "The rules can always be amended to allay any concern on that count. The rules have the same power as the law. If necessary, we can go a step further to change the law itself."The DPDP Act has been been justified in citing citizen's right to privacy, the need to protect data and in placing obligations on data fiduciaries.Centre's reaction came days after the apex court agreed to examine a plea filed by Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) which represents 21 of India's leading news media organisations and challenged the validity of various provisions of the act and rules framed under it.The association alleged that the law was violative of the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression and threatened the full spectrum of journalistic activity.Officials said that the the concern about the DPDP act becoming an impediment for journalists will be addressed by carving out exemptions for them in the rules and, if necessary, in the law itself.I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnav said on Friday that Section 7 of the DPDP Act is for data fiduciaries like banks, telecom providers and insurance companies and media does not come within its ambit. "This govt is committed to uphold the constitutionally guaranteed rights to freedom and expression". Section 7 says that "the personal data of a data principal may be processed by a data fiduciary (a) for the specified purpose for which the Data Principal has voluntarily provided her personal data. .. and in respect of which she has not indicated... that she does not consent to the use of her personal data."
Article Summary: Centre open to amending DPDP Act rules or the law itself to address media concerns over its impact on press freedom, days after Supreme Court agreed to hear challenge. Senior officials at the ministry for electronics & information technology said that sections of the law are applicable to data fiduciaries and they are not for journalists.

Article Title: 'No' to peace bond, 'yes' to INDIA bloc: Has Neha Bora outsmarted CJP leaders?
Article Text:
AISA president Neha Bora and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke

Neha Bora on why she would not sign peace bond

Neha Bora, along with Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, during the opposition's protest.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: When Neha Bora recently said “AISA will not be a part of normalising the signing of peace bonds”, she inadvertently highlighted a contrast that the Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests against SIR and "vote chori" had brought to the fore. Neha’s refusal to sign the peace bond before a special executive magistrate and her subsequent challenge to the police move drew an obvious parallel. Did the CJP leaders - Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Sourav Das - give in to peace bond pressure easily?“Peace bonds are being weaponised to curb democratic protests. Signing such peace bonds is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,” the AISA national president said and claimed that she was detained within 10 minutes of protesting at Mandi House on October 16 and was told that she and other protesters were in breach of peace.“On one side, the Constitution gives us the right to dissent. On the other hand, such peace bonds are invoked only to detain people in the name of breach of peace. Therefore, signing such peace bonds is a principally wrong decision for us. It is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,” Bora said defending her decision.Bora has still not signed the bond and is awaiting copies of 6 FIRs cited as her criminal antecedents in peace-bond proceedings.This, after she insisted for all documents relied upon in the show-cause notice seeking execution of her peace bond.Now, let’s rewind to October 10.The CJP’s call for Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10 had, as expected, evoked great national interest and anticipation. All eyes were on Abhijeet Dipke and his associates Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who had in June-July this year led a successful youth mobilisation against NEET paper leak. The CJP-led protests had ensured that Dharmendra Pradhan was forced to resign as Union education minister. After all, they were the new heroes of GenZ, who had left the politicians far behind.But ahead of October 10, the national capital saw an unprecedented clampdown. The Delhi Police closed down anything and everything that could facilitate the movement of protesters to Jantar Mantar. For the CJP leadership, the message was loud and clear - they will not get a free passage, unlike in June when they were allowed to gather and mobilise youth at Jantar Mantar for their protests against NEET paper leak.But October 10 morning started with an anticlimax. The top 3 CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das travelled together from Mumbai to Delhi and were detained from aircraft as soon as they landed in the national capital. Thousands of protesters who had responded to their calls, braved the police clampdown. They were all detained.The CJP leaders were released a day later after giving an undertaking to maintain public order. Delhi Police said a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished for CJP activists Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das for maintaining peace and good behaviour for one year, following their preventive arrest on October 10.The CJP leaders made two more attempts to reclaim the streets - when Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka tried to reach Jantar Mantar and again when Dipke urged people to join the "Lehra Do Tiranga" march with the national flag at Central Park in Connaught Place.However, they were detained again and made to sign peace bonds to come out of detention. And while the CJP leaders failed to recreate the magic of Jantar Mantar 1.0, AISA leader Neha Bora took the centrestage. The AISA national president was detained 5 times between October 2 and October 11. However, every time she was released, she would come back to the streets and continue with her protests.During the peak of the protests, Neha Bora hogged the headlines for foxing the police. On October 11, Neha Bora announced a gathering at RK Ashram Marg Metro Station around 2:30pm as part of demonstrations heading toward central Delhi and Jantar Mantar.Heavy police deployment and barricades were set up around RK Ashram Marg to prevent demonstrators from moving toward Jantar Mantar. During the confrontation, police mistakenly chased and detained another protester whose face was partially covered, believing her to be Neha Bora.While police attention was focused at RK Ashram Marg, Neha Bora surfaced near Connaught Place (CP), breaching barricades and running alongside fellow demonstrators in a dash that went viral on social media.Little wonder then, when a user on X called Neha Bora "more talented" than CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and described her as a "complete GenZ icon", Dipke responded simply: "I agree." The X user had posted: "Maturity is realizing Neha Bora is more talented than Abhijeet Dipke. A complete GenZ icon with an absolutely ridiculous aura.” It was a comparison that manifested all along the “vote chori” protests.Neha Bora was on the streets every time she was released from detention by the police. She was everywhere - with the CJP leadership, the social activists and also the politicians. When Rahul Gandhi chose to walk behind her during one of the protest marches of INDIA bloc, it spoke volumes about the impact she had made with her street politics. Clearly, the campaign against “vote chori” had put the spotlight on Neha Bora, even as the CJP struggled to find their way to the centre stage of the protests.For the CJP, it was a harsh realisation that a lot had changed between July and October. Unlike the anti-NEET paper leak protests in June-July, the Congress-led INDIA bloc this time around were already on the streets demanding resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Interestingly, while the INDIA bloc’s original protest schedule had only one announced street protest on October 6, the group returned back to the streets four days in a row till October 9, which was a day before the announced CJP protest.The CJP and the Congress had stayed away from each other during the anti-NEET protests. After Jantar Mantar 1.0 was over, the 'cockroaches' carried out their own campaigns in different states, while the Congress shifted focus to protests against SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Abhijeet Dipke has announced that he has no political plans and would prefer to keep CJP as a pressure group. So when CJP announced support for INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally, it set tongues wagging about their political ambitions.With CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0 not shaping out as they would have hoped, perhaps its leadership should take a leaf out of Saurav Das’s advice on X to a Congress “soldier” who had questioned why youth Congress and NSUI activists were being detained as soon as they hit the streets and cockroaches were allowed to roam free. Responding to him, CJP co-founder Saurav Das had then said: “if u guys r detained immediately, then u must rethink ur strategy. don’t blame others for ur failures.”The context of that remark was different and CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0 campaign was in no way a failure, but Sourav's take on “rethinking strategy” perhaps holds true for the cockroaches at present.
Article Summary: Neha Bora's refusal to sign peace bond drew an obvious parallel with the Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests against SIR and "vote chori" The AISA national president was detained 5 times between October 2 and October 11. She has still not signed the bond and is awaiting copies of 6 FIRs cited as her criminal antecedents.

Article Title: End of SIR doesn't mean freezing of voters list: SC

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday said completion of special intensive revision (SIR) does not mean electoral rolls have been frozen, a statement that would put to rest the apprehension that names removed from draft rolls cannot be restored to the voters' list and such persons are rendered permanently disabled from exercising their franchise.Hearing petitions challenging SIR in UP, Kerala and Chhattisgarh, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to extend the deadline. The top court asked EC to respond to the plea as well as Ramachandran's note.

Article Title: Isro’s GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission successful: Next-generation navigation satellite placed in orbit; NavIC constellation gets a boost
Article Text:
It was the 20th flight of the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle. (Photo by C Suresh Kumar)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRIHARIKOTA: India's regional satellite navigation system, NavIC , which was facing a shortage of operational satellites, got a boost with the successful launch of NVS-03 on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday by Indian Space Research Organisation ( Isro ).GSLV-F18 carrying 2,250kg next-generation navigation satellite -- NVS-03 -- lifted off from the second launch pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) in Sriharikota at 11.51pm on Friday, as scheduled. It was the 20th flight of the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV). Around 18 minutes later, NVS-03 satellite was placed in a geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) of 37,023km apogee and 170km perigee."The rocket has successfully and precisely placed the satellite into its intended elliptical orbit. It achieved a 170km perigee and 38,080km apogee. This is the 5th mission from Sriharikota this year. GSLV has carried 34 tonnes of spacecraft to space so far. We achieved this mission with a turnaround time of just 56 days after the GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission in September. With this launch, we have restored NavIC constellation operation as we need a minimum of four satellites to perform positioning, navigation and timing services," said Isro chairman V Narayanan.He said, “The satellite is healthy, and the solar panel has been deployed. Already three pyro walls are operated, and we have lifted. Every system is totally healthy, and we are going to continue the operation and place the satellite in the intended circular orbit.”NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro's next-generation navigation satellite system, designed to ensure continuity of services under the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS), operationally known as NavIC. The satellite carries an indigenously developed atomic clock along with procured atomic clocks. It also carries the L1 frequency signal in addition to the existing L5 and S-band signals.NavIC is India's independent regional satellite navigation system, designed to provide positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services across the country and an area extending approximately 1,500km beyond the Indian landmass. The additional L1 signal, alongside the existing signals, is expected to improve compatibility with other satellite navigation systems and widen the potential use of NavIC in civilian applications.The NVS-03 mission is part of Isro's plan to deploy five second-generation navigation satellites -- NVS-01 to NVS-05 -- to augment the existing NavIC constellation and improve continuity and reliability of navigation services.The launch assumes significance as NavIC was unable to provide standalone positioning services because of a shortage of operational satellites. In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on July 29, Union minister of state for space Jitendra Singh said the constellation had only three satellites providing positioning, navigation and timing services, against the minimum four required for basic positioning services. While its timing service remains functional, the addition of NVS-03, once commissioned, could help restore standalone positioning capability."Since NavIC is being used in a multi-constellation environment for most of the use cases, there is no vulnerability for the users. The next NavIC satellite, NVS-03, is ready for launch and two more satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, are in an advanced stage of realisation," the minister had said then.The setback to the constellation followed the failure of NVS-02, launched on Jan 29, 2025, to complete its orbit-raising manoeuvres. An Isro review committee found that an electrical signal had failed to reach a pyro valve in the satellite's oxidiser line, preventing the propulsion system from firing and the satellite from reaching its intended orbit. The failure prompted Isro to undertake corrective measures for subsequent missions.The first satellite in the second-generation series, NVS-01, was launched aboard the GSLV-F12 on May 29, 2023. It was also the first satellite in the series to carry an indigenous atomic clock.The Isro chief said five more launches are planned this financial year. “We are moving closer to Gaganyaan G1 uncrewed flight,” he added.
Article Summary: The launch assumes significance as NavIC was unable to provide standalone positioning services because of a shortage of operational satellites. The satellite carries an indigenously developed atomic clock along with procured atomic clocks. It also carries the L1 frequency signal in addition to the existing L5 and S-band signals.

NEW DELHI: Congress's Rahul Gandhi and finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman sparred on social media over govt's decision to sell its stake in IDBI Bank with the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha backing protesting employees.A day after he wrote to "members of the IDBI bank family", Rahul accused govt of selling banks in contrast to banks being established during Congress's tenure."During Congress' time, IDBI was established - to build the nation's industry. Article Title: Census 2027 population enumeration phase to be of record 50 days

NEW DELHI: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 will last longer than in past census exercises, with its duration spanning nearly one-and-a-half months from Jan 10 to Feb 28, including the 15-day self-enumeration window, as against the earlier Phase-2 duration of 20 days, conventionally running from Feb 9-28.Sources told TOI that the house-to-house population enumeration schedule announced earlier for poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab also spans 35 days. The longer duration may be linked to the increased number of questions at 40, including pertaining to caste, to be asked in Phase-2 of Census 2027, as against 29 in 2011.No census has been declared in Manipur. The census exercise in the state was put on hold after demands from various sections within the state that the National Register of Citizens (NRC) exercise be conducted first.A notification issued by the Union home ministry Friday declared that a nationwide census of population shall be undertaken - except in Manipur (till further declaration); poll-bound states of Goa, UP, Punjab and Uttarakhand, where it was preponed in view of the impending assembly elections early next year; and UT of Ladakh and snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of Himachal Pradesh and UT of Jammu & Kashmir, where it has already been completed - from Jan 25 to Feb 27, 2027.This shall be preceded by a window of self-enumeration from Jan 10-24. Article Title: India's poverty will be down from 14.2% to 12.1% in 2 years: World Bank
Article Text:
World Bank projects India's poverty rate to fall to 12.1% by 2028, from 14.2% in 2026, citing strong consumption growth and rising employment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: World Bank has said that poverty in India, defined at $4.2 a day, will decline from 14.2% in 2026 to 12.1% by 2028.Between 2011 and 2023, it is estimated that the share of the population living below $4.2 a day declined from 57.7% to 16.1%, lifting an estimated 496 million people out of poverty. It said that extreme poverty ($3 a day) declined from 27.1% to 2.6% during this period."This progress was mainly driven by strong consumption growth; rising employment, especially among women; and expanded social transfers, including food subsidies. As poverty declined, it became increasingly concentrated among households with lower education, fewer assets, limited access to stable employment, and higher dependency ratios. Wage disparities, however, remain pronounced, as median earnings among the top 10% of workers were about 13 times those of the bottom 10% in 2023," World Bank said in its latest Poverty & Equity brief.Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman cheered the decline in poverty in the country, pointing out that the report recognised India's progress as a country with one of the fastest poverty declines in the world."Under the leadership of PM Narendra Modi, govt's sustained policy efforts are yielding tangible results, strengthening the foundations for inclusive growth and greater economic opportunity.This is the reason why NDA govt wins people's trust and mandate of our citizens. We remain committed to building on this progress through productive employment, stronger household incomes and effective delivery of public services, so that aspirations of our people are met," she posted on X.World Bank also noted that between 2017 and 2023, employment increased by about 134 million people, nearly twice the growth of the working-age population, with major gains driven by rural women entering paid work and raising the number of earners in households."Labour market conditions continue to be broadly resilient, with labour force participation and employment rates stable between Q1 FY 2026 and Q1 FY 2027. However, youth unemployment rose from 14.6% to 15.9% between the two quarters, particularly among rural young women. Moreover, real earnings remained broadly unchanged with employment growth concentrated in relatively low-productivity activities," it said.
Article Summary: World Bank projects India's poverty rate to fall to 12.1% by 2028, from 14.2% in 2026. It cites strong consumption growth and rising employment, especially among women. As poverty declined, it became increasingly concentrated among households with lower education and fewer assets.

Article Title: Discourage weaponisation of rape law in relationships gone sour: SC
Article Text:
Supreme Court warns against misuse of rape laws after consensual relationships turn sour, saying breakups cannot retrospectively criminalise consensual sex

NEW DELHI: Society and courts must discourage weaponisation of criminal law against men in the aftermath of an emotional discord and breakup of a consenting romantic relationship, Supreme Court said Friday, expressing concern over the disturbing trend of criminal provision of rape being invoked to prosecute men after relationship turns sour.A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said the legislature never intended consensual sexual acts between adults to be retrospectively criminalised merely because the relationship came to an end. "It is unfortunate that despite judicial deprecation, this trend is increasing, and it is a matter of concern as often settlement of disputes come with huge monetary considerations to be borne by the male accused," it said.The court underlined "a worrying trend in recent years, wherein consensual relationship is given a colour of sexual assault"."In fact, such an approach denudes the man of any agency entirely, as the mere factum of being in a consensual relationship at one point would bind him to it entirely for fear of being accused of rape at a subsequent point of time," SC said, while allowing the plea of a man who was being prosecuted for rape on a complaint filed by his erstwhile live-in partner with whom he shared a relationship for seven years..The top court also cautioned that the trend carries the risk of undermining the gravity of the serious criminal offence of rape.
Article Summary: Supreme Court expresses concern over disturbing trend of criminal provision of rape being invoked to prosecute men after relationship turns sour. Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said legislature never intended consensual sexual acts between adults to be retrospectively criminalised.

Article Title: Paid to hire, paid to work: Inside India’s Rs 99,446 cr plan to reshape the formal workforce
Article Text:
The government aims to create more than 3.5 crore jobs over two years, including 1.92 crore first-time employees.

Where are India’s jobs?

Distribution of India's workforce

Why manufacturing is central

Looking Through Employment Elasticities

What employers receive, and what startups need to know

Your eligibility, as an employer, for the scheme.

For employees earning below Rs 10,000, it is 10 per cent of wages, up to Rs 1,000.

For those earning more than Rs 10,000 and up to Rs 20,000, it is Rs 2,000.

For those earning above Rs 20,000, it is Rs 3,000, subject to the gross-wage ceiling.

What first-time employees receive

Benefits for first-time employees.

Can the incentives create additional jobs?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) is a central government scheme designed to encourage formal employment by offering financial incentives to both employers and employees. It provides money to first-time workers entering jobs covered by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), while also rewarding companies that expand their workforce and retain new hires.Approved by the Union Cabinet on July 1, 2025, the scheme has a total outlay of Rs 99,446 crore.PMVBRY has two components. Under Part A, eligible first-time employees receive a one-time incentive equivalent to one month’s EPF wage, capped at Rs 15,000.Part B provides incentives to employers who create additional jobs. Eligible employers can receive up to Rs 3,000 per month for each qualifying additional employee. The scheme covers eligible jobs created between August 1, 2025 and July 31, 2027. Manufacturing establishments receive support for four years, compared with two years for employers in other sectors.The government aims to incentivise more than 3.5 crore jobs over two years, including 1.92 crore first-time employees.These are government targets, not independent estimates of jobs expected to be created.The scheme addresses a structural weakness in India's employment landscape: the limited availability of regular, salaried work.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation's Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) for 2025, 56.2 per cent of India's workers are self-employed and another 20.2 per cent are engaged in casual labour. Regular wage or salaried employment accounts for just 23.6 per cent of the workforce.The challenge, therefore, extends beyond reducing unemployment. It is also about expanding access to stable, formal jobs that offer workers social security and a more predictable source of income. PMVBRY is the government's attempt to encourage that transition.The PLFS Annual Report 2025 estimated that India had 61.6 crore employed people aged 15 and above.Agriculture remained the largest employer, accounting for 43 per cent of workers. Manufacturing accounted for 12.1 per cent, construction 12 per cent, trade, hotels and restaurants 12.9 per cent, transport, storage and communications 5.8 per cent, and other services 13.1 per cent. Mining and quarrying accounted for 0.3 per cent, while electricity, water and related services made up 0.7 per cent.Grouped broadly, the figures put around 43.3 per cent of workers in the primary sector, including agriculture and mining. Another 24.8 per cent are in the secondary sector, including manufacturing, utilities and construction, and 31.8 per cent in the tertiary sector, including trade, transport and other services. These are employment shares, not shares of GDP or GVA.Employment status adds another dimension. In 2025, 56.2 per cent of workers were self-employed, 23.6 per cent were in regular wage or salaried employment and 20.2 per cent were casual labourers. The unemployment rate for people aged 15 and above was 3.1 per cent under the survey’s usual-status measure, while it was 9.9 per cent among people aged 15 to 29.Year-on-year comparisons need caution. The ministry revised the PLFS sampling design in January 2025 and shifted the annual reference period from July–June to January–December. It advises care when comparing the new series with earlier reports. The reported fall in agriculture’s share from 44.8 per cent in 2024 to 43 per cent in 2025, and the rise in manufacturing from 11.6 per cent to 12.1 per cent, are not conclusive evidence of a structural shift.PMVBRY targets a narrower problem: formal payroll employment recorded through EPFO. It is not an employment guarantee and does not directly address self-employment, casual work or agricultural underemployment.PMVBRY covers eligible establishments across sectors but gives manufacturing employers a longer incentive period. Its official guidelines say the scheme is intended to complement the National Manufacturing Mission by promoting new industries and expanding existing ones, particularly in labour-intensive manufacturing.Under the revised national-accounts series with 2022–23 as the base year, manufacturing accounted for 14.7 per cent of GVA in 2022–23 and 2023–24, and 14.8 per cent in provisional estimates for 2025–26, according to the ministry of statistics and programme implementation. The figures are not directly comparable with estimates under the previous base year.The employment picture is distinct. PLFS 2025 put manufacturing’s share of workers at 12.1 per cent. Separately, the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) results for 2023–24 reported that employment in covered manufacturing establishments rose 5.92 per cent over the previous year, reaching nearly 1.96 crore persons engaged. The ASI covers registered manufacturing establishments within its survey scope, not every manufacturing worker in India.A working paper by Sangeeta Ghosh at the Institute for Studies in Industrial Development,, found employment elasticities above 0.5 in many of the 55 organised manufacturing industries it studied for the period from the mid-2000s. Employment elasticity measures the relationship between output growth and employment growth. However, the paper also found that more than 40 per cent of new employment generated between 2008 and 2017–18 was contract employment. It focuses on organised manufacturing, so its findings cannot automatically be applied to the whole sector.The four-year incentive window signals the government’s view that manufacturing, particularly labour-intensive segments, can generate sustained employment. The National Manufacturing Mission, announced in the 2025–26 Union Budget, is part of the wider push.Under Part B, employers can receive up to Rs 3,000 a month for each additional employee whose gross wages at joining are up to Rs 1 lakh, subject to the scheme’s conditions. The incentive covers eligible first-time employees and re-joiners. The amount depends on EPF wages:The incentive is paid in six-monthly lump sums after the relevant six months of employment and electronic challan-cum-return filings. The employee must stay with the same employer for at least six months, with contributions received for that period. Employers must also maintain a minimum net additional-employment threshold. Those with a baseline below 50 employees must add at least two, while those with a baseline of 50 or more must add at least five. Incentives do not accrue for months when the applicable threshold is not met.The baseline is central to eligibility. For existing EPFO-registered employers, it is based on average employment during the relevant period before the scheme. For new establishments registered with EPFO between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027, the baseline is fixed at 20 employees. Only qualifying additional jobs above that baseline and beyond the applicable hiring threshold can count towards the incentive.Startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) do not receive a separate incentive rate or automatic exemption from these rules. They can benefit if they are eligible establishments, comply with EPFO filing requirements and create qualifying additional employment. A new establishment with a baseline of 20, for instance, cannot claim the employer incentive merely by hiring a few people while remaining below the baseline and threshold.Consider an eligible employee with EPF wages of Rs 18,000, for whom the monthly incentive would be Rs 2,000. If the employer meets the hiring test and remains eligible for all 24 months, the notional incentive for that employee would be Rs 48,000. For a manufacturing establishment, the incentive can continue for 48 months, making the corresponding maximum Rs 96,000. These are illustrative calculations, not guaranteed payouts.Part A supports first-time employees earning up to Rs 1 lakh a month with an incentive equivalent to one month’s EPF wage, capped at Rs 15,000. The first instalment, capped at Rs 7,500, is payable after six completed months. The second follows 12 months of service and completion of a financial-literacy programme. A portion of it is placed in a savings instrument or deposit account.The central question surrounding PMVBRY is whether lowering the cost of hiring will persuade companies to create jobs they would not otherwise have offered.Employment subsidies carry an inherent risk: governments may end up paying companies for recruitment that would have happened anyway. There is also the possibility that employers could replace existing workers with eligible employees to qualify for incentives. These are recognised risks in evaluating employment subsidies, not evidence that such practices have occurred under PMVBRY.The government's initial implementation figures offer an indication of the scheme's reach. In a backgrounder published on August 1, 2026, the Press Information Bureau said more than 72 lakh first-time employees had joined the formal workforce since August 2025. Nearly 30 per cent of the beneficiaries were women, while more than 15 lakh beneficiaries had received employment-linked incentives.These are government-reported figures.PMVBRY is an attempt to use public money to make formal hiring more attractive, with manufacturing receiving a longer period of support. But the scale of enrolment and the amount of incentives disbursed will not, by themselves, establish whether the policy has succeeded.The real test will be whether the scheme creates additional jobs, whether those jobs offer stable employment and whether employers retain workers after government support runs out. For India, the challenge is not simply to move more people onto formal payrolls, but to ensure that the jobs they enter are productive, secure and sustainable.
Article Summary: The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) is a central government scheme designed to encourage formal employment. It provides money to first-time workers entering jobs covered by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), while rewarding companies that expand their workforce and retain new hires. The scheme covers eligible jobs created between August 1, 2025 and July 31, 2027.
