Article Title: 30% in 2019, cancer drug margins at 700% now
Article Text:
Anti-cancer drugs show mark-ups of up to 700% despite NPPA's 2019 price curbs, raising questions over one-time price cuts

Evidence shows 1-time caps give limited relief: Activist group

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A look at the mark-up on some of the drugs on which National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) put a trade margin cap of 30% on selling price in Feb 2019 shows that a majority had mark-ups of 100%-700% in the Authority's 2026 list. Citing this data, the All-India Drug Action Network, which works on access to affordable medicines, pointed out the futility of one-time MRP reduction as a policy measure in the absence of a mandate to maintain permanent margin caps along with consistent monitoring.Of the 137 anti-cancer drugs that NPPA listed for reduction of trade margin, 34 are from the 2019 NPPA list of 42 anti-cancer drugs. However, the recent list put out by NPPA, showing steep reduction in MRP, reveals that most drugs from the 2019 list that feature in the 2026 list have breached the 43% mark-up level. This level is equivalent to a 30% trade margin because while the margin is calculated as a percentage of the final MRP, the mark-up is a percentage of the price to the stockist.The mark-up in 2026 prior to the latest order was higher than it was even before the 2019 order and hence the percentage reduction in prices too is much higher in most cases now compared to seven years back. However, in the case of drugs which saw very steep reduction in MRP in 2019, the percentage reduction is lower in 2026.For example, the MRP of a brand of an anti-cancer drug Pemetrexed fell from Rs 7,000 to Rs 800 in 2019. In the latest MRP reduction, it has fallen from Rs 1,095 to Rs 297, a more modest reduction than in 2019. Many multinationals which reduced the MRP by significant amounts in 2019 have done little or no reduction this time and some originator companies - those that held the patent for the medicine originally - did not slash the MRP by much on either occasion.Only five brands from the 2019 list had a mark-up of 43% prior to the latest order, another four had mark-ups ranging from 43% to 100%. The mark-up on the remaining 39 ranged from 100% to over 700%."NPPA is calling it trade margin capping, as they did in 2019 also. That's misleading because it is not a cap. It is just a one-time reduction of MRP by restriction of the mark-up," said Malini Aisola of AIDAN adding that this would not be enough to prevent mark-ups rising again as happened after 2019.
Article Summary: A look at the mark-up on some of the drugs on which National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) put a trade margin cap of 30% on selling price in Feb 2019 shows that a majority had mark-ups of 100%-700% in the Authority's 2026 list. The All-India Drug Action Network, which works on access to affordable medicines, pointed out the futility of one-time MRP reduction as a policy measure.

Article Title: MLC election results: BJP wins big, but Congress and Samajwadi Party send a message from Nagpur, Varanasi
Article Text:
BJP's big win in MLC elections comes with setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi

BJP-led NDA secured 16 of the 28 MLC seats across four states, while the SP won five seats in Uttar Pradesh and Congress retained Nagpur in Maharashtra.

BJP mocks Congress over 'zero' seats

BJP president Nitin Nabin targeted Congress over its poor performance in the MLC elections, pointing out that voting had taken place using ballot papers.

Nagpur win gives Congress a chance to respond

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned the BJP's setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi after PM Modi mocked the party's performance in the MLC elections.

Varanasi setback gives SP a boost ahead of 2027

What do the results mean for 2027?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The MLC elections across four states brought both shock and cheer for the BJP and Congress. While the Congress suffered a humiliating defeat in Karnataka, where it is in power but failed to win a single seat, the BJP faltered in two constituencies which mattered the most. One being Nagpur, which is home to the RSS headquarters, and Varanasi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency.The BJP nevertheless emerged as the largest party, winning 13 of the 28 seats contested, while its allies took the NDA's tally to 16. The alliance swept all four seats in Karnataka, won six of the 11 seats in Uttar Pradesh and secured four of the eight seats in Bihar. In Maharashtra, the ruling Mahayuti won two of the five seats, while the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi secured three.The Congress's only victory came from Nagpur, a political stronghold of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari. In Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party retained the Varanasi Teachers' constituency and was heading towards victory in the Graduates' seat, both of which it had won in 2020.What began as celebrations and sharp jibes at the Congress on Wednesday turned into a war of words on Thursday, as the results in Nagpur and Varanasi gave the opposition grounds to question the BJP's claims of electoral dominance.As the early results came in on Wednesday, BJP leaders targeted the Congress over its poor performance, particularly in Karnataka, where the party is in power but failed to win a single seat.PM Modi took a swipe at the opposition party on X, pointing out that voting in the four states had taken place using ballot papers."Guess how many seats Congress won?" he asked.The remark came amid the Congress's repeated allegations over electronic voting machines and its demand for a return to ballot-paper voting.BJP president Nitin Nabin also targeted the Congress, saying the party had failed to win public support despite voting being conducted using ballot papers."The people are repeatedly rejecting Congress' anarchist politics," Nabin said, adding that public trust remained with PM Modi irrespective of whether elections were conducted using EVMs or ballot papers.BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also attacked Rahul Gandhi over his allegations of vote theft"Kamchori ki aadat chhodiye. Vote chori ka shabd apke muh se khud chhoot jayega," he said, asking the Congress leader to give up what he described as a habit of avoiding hard work.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJP's Sudhakar Kohale to retain the Nagpur Division Graduates' constituency after more than 40 hours of counting.Kohale had initially taken the lead before Wanjari overtook him through preferential votes.Nagpur is important for the BJP. Besides housing the RSS headquarters, it is associated with Fadnavis and Gadkari, both of whom campaigned for Kohale.The Congress had wrested the seat from the BJP in 2020, when Wanjari defeated Sandip Joshi. By retaining it in 2026, the party prevented the BJP from reclaiming a constituency it had dominated for decades.The Maharashtra Congress also targeted Fadnavis over a social media post in which he had claimed that the party had failed to win a single seat.Sharing a screenshot of what it said was a deleted post by Fadnavis, the party accused him of celebrating before counting was complete. The post had described the Congress's performance as a "big fat zero".The Congress said Fadnavis had been forced to delete the post after the Nagpur result and warned that the outcome was only a trailer of future political battles.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh also responded to PM Modi's remarks, questioning the BJP's losses in Nagpur and Varanasi."The Prime Minister needs to introspect, but instead, he's lecturing others! Before counting Congress's seats, I wish he'd also reflect on why the BJP lost both seats in his own parliamentary constituency of Varanasi, and how Congress managed to defeat the BJP in RSS's stronghold of Nagpur?" Ramesh said."Mr. Modi, stop the trolling," he added, accusing the government of failing to address inflation, unemployment and weak private investment.Ramesh claimed that voters in Varanasi, Nagpur, Lucknow, Prayagraj and Patna had expressed dissatisfaction with the Centre's policies.The BJP's biggest setback in Uttar Pradesh came from Varanasi, where the Samajwadi Party retained the Teachers' seat and established an unassailable lead in the Graduates' constituency.The BJP retained six of the 11 seats contested in the state, while the SP won four and was heading towards a fifth.The SP had won both Varanasi seats in 2020 as well. Six years later, the BJP has failed to dislodge the party from either constituency despite its strong presence in the region.Although the two MLC constituencies cover a wider geographical area than PM Modi's Lok Sabha seat, the results carry political significance given Varanasi's association with the Prime Minister since 2014.They also come after PM Modi's victory margin in Varanasi declined from nearly 4.8 lakh votes in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections to around 1.5 lakh in 2024.Across Uttar Pradesh, the SP's tally is set to rise from three seats in 2020 to five, while the BJP has retained its tally of six.The SP had also emerged as the largest party in Uttar Pradesh in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, winning 37 of the state's 80 parliamentary seats against the BJP's 33.BJP deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya acknowledged that the party had expected a better performance."These elections are decided by highly educated and qualified voters. The BJP has repeated its previous performance, but we expected to win more seats. We will examine why we fell short," Maurya said.The SP, meanwhile, has repeatedly accused the BJP of electoral irregularities, allegations the ruling party has rejected.On polling day, Akhilesh Yadav had claimed that the BJP was attempting to influence even the MLC elections, which have a limited electorate."If the BJP can do this in MLC polls for teachers and graduate constituencies where a limited number of people cast votes, one can imagine their preparation for the assembly polls," he had said.The NDA's overall tally shows that the BJP and its allies remain ahead in these Legislative Council contests. But the results in Nagpur and Varanasi also show that the party has struggled to regain certain seats despite its strong presence in both regions.In Uttar Pradesh, the SP and Congress are preparing to contest the 2027 assembly elections together, hoping to build on their performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.The alliance won 43 of the state's 80 parliamentary seats in 2024, reducing the BJP's tally from 62 in 2019 to 33. Akhilesh Yadav has said the alliance will continue in 2027, although the two parties still need to settle their seat-sharing arrangement.The MLC results, however, cannot be treated as an indication of how the state will vote in the assembly elections. These contests involve a limited electorate of registered graduates and teachers, unlike assembly polls, which are decided by a much wider voter base.For the BJP, which is seeking a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh, the challenge will be to counter the opposition's gains. For the SP-Congress alliance, the question is whether it can repeat its 2024 Lok Sabha performance when the state's 403 assembly seats go to the polls in 2027.

Article Title: UK govt announces new ‘safe and legal’ routes for refugees in India to resettle in UK
Article Text:
UK announces three new refugee resettlement routes for people in India and six other countries, allowing sponsorship through charities, employers and universities.

TOI correspondent from London:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a bid to dissuade asylum-seekers from arriving in Britain on the backs of lorries or via small boats, the UK home office has announced three new “safe and legal” sponsorship routes for refugees in India and six other countries to come to the UK and claim asylum.The new routes are initially targeted at refugees who have sought protection in India, Bangladesh, Egypt, Kenya, Malaysia, Pakistan and Uganda.To be eligible, the refugees will need to be outside their country of nationality, to have been verified by the UNHCR as meeting the definition of refugee and to have registered with the UNHCR or relevant authorities in one of these seven countries before Oct 1. So, in India’s case, it could be Tibetans, Sri Lankan Tamils, Afghans, Rohingya and others from Myanmar, who could be eligible for these routes, but not Indian nationals residing in India, nor internally displaced people.The refugee sponsorship routes, modelled on a similar programme in Canada, allow sponsors in the UK to identify refugees they wish to sponsor. The new routes are named community sponsorship, which enables UK charities to identify refugees they wish to sponsor; refugee work, which enables UK employers to sponsor and provide refugees jobs; and refugee study, which enables UK universities to sponsor refugees to study in the UK.Once resettled, the refugees will have an immediate right to work, study and to access welfare benefits in Britain and be placed on a five-year path to permanent resettlement.Sponsors will have to finance and provide their accommodation, the aim being to reduce the amount UK’s govt spends on asylum hotels.Applications to be sponsors for the community and study route have opened and the first arrivals are expected in autumn 2027. Applications under the work route will open in spring 2027.Both Reform UK and the Conservatives vowed to shut the scheme if they come to power. Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said until illegal migration is stopped, “we should not be creating new routes into the UK for asylum claimants”.
Article Summary: UK announces three new refugee resettlement routes for people in India and six other countries, allowing sponsorship through charities, employers and universities. The routes are initially targeted at refugees who have sought protection in India, Bangladesh, Egypt, Kenya, Malaysia, Pakistan and Uganda. The refugees will have an immediate right to work, study and to access welfare benefits in Britain.

Article Title: Uttarakhand chopper flying: A lot has changed for better, but a lot remains to be done
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Hours after seven people on board an Aryan Aviation chopper died when it crashed near Gaurikund on June 15, 2025, the aviation ministry had found two helicopters of Trans Bharat — whose chopper crashed on Friday — were airborne “under unsuitable weather conditions. ” It had suspended the licences of both Trans Bharat pilots for six months.While the cause of Trans Bharat’s Friday crash in which six people lost their lives will be known once the inquiry report is out, there have been red flags regarding this and several other chopper operators in the hill region. The Uttarakhand govt has grounded Trans Bharat fleet for now.Aviation industry insiders point out that six days before Friday crash, another Trans Bharat helicopter carrying five pilgrims from Sahastradhara to Kedarnath via Guptkashi had made an emergency landing at Baurari stadium on Oct 24 “where children were playing.” Luckily all six, five passengers and the pilot, were safe that day and the chopper took off soon again.“On May 20, 2026, a Trans Bharat Bell 407 flying from Badrinath to Dehradun with seven people on board ran into severe downdrafts over the Chamba–Arakot sector of Tehri Garhwal. During the emergency landing that followed, its tail struck a 33 kV high-tension line. The pilot, a former IAF pilot, got everyone down uninjured,” said sources.Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) is probing this case.The Char Dham corridor has no single agency answerable for safety. While the DGCA licenses the operators and pilots, UCADA runs the helipads, sets slots and manages shuttle operations. The Sanjay Kumar Jha-headed parliamentary standing committee on transport, tourism and culture had in Aug 2025 called this arrangement “inherently unsafe and unsustainable.” It said there was a “responsibility vacuum” between the two agencies. It found that the DGCA was acting as a passive licensing authority. It also noted that India still has no mandatory, terrain-specific mountain-flying training or certification for pilots operating in the Himalaya.This changed significantly after last summer following a spate of chopper crashes in Uttarakhand. Air traffic control units are being set up, with Kedarnath having one now and Badrinath to get a unti soon. Routes have been defined in the region and take offs are both restricted in number and controlled in a defined pattern with some gap. This is a far cry from the almost unregulated chopper movement in the hill region till last summer.“System wise there has been a lot of improvement. The Char Dham Operations are quite extensive in every aspect. From commercial to maintenance and from operations to ATC, every department is working very hard to ensure safety and efficiency is achieved. After the season of 2025 , there are many different measures that are implemented to ensure highest safety standards are met. These include ATC at Sahastradhara and Sitapur to ensure that flying is well coordinated and controlled,” said Captain Nitin Welde, a senior chopper pilot who operates in Uttarakhand.“There’s a fuel bowser at Sahastradhara to ensure that IOCL supplies fuel in best possible manner. Take off and landing tarmac is separated from parking Tarmac to ensure orderly flow of positioning. There are CCTV cameras all across valley which give feed through a mobile app. All can get a live feed as regards weather valley. For higher helipads above 10,000 feet, the weight limitations are in place and that ensures higher reserve of power while landing and take off. Training for pilots has increased since last year. And there is adequate training in Char Dham sector as well as Kedar shuttles. The DGCA FOIs have been visiting the valley on a weekly basis and UCADA ops department is fully involved in a minute to minute monitoring and support,” added Captain Welde.“Friday was a sad day where it appears that weather in exit phase of Badri valley wasn’t good,” Captain Welde said.
Article Summary: The cause of Trans Bharat’s Friday crash in which six people lost their lives will be known once the inquiry report is out. There have been red flags regarding this and several other chopper operators in the hill region. The Uttarakhand govt has grounded Trans Bharats fleet for now.

NEW DELHI: The six people on board a helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation died after it crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Friday afternoon. The helicopter was travelling from Badrinath to Dehradun when it crashed into a hillside near Chai village."All six people on board chopper that crashed in Joshimath have died, their bodies found," Chamoli Superintendent of Police Surjit Singh Panwar told PTI.The helicopter took off from Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1.14 pm. Authorities lost track of it while it was crossing the Joshimath Valley and it was subsequently reported missing near Hathi Parvat.Search and rescue teams, including personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the Army, police and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), were deployed to the area following reports of the crash.According to the available details, six people were on board the helicopter, including the pilot and five passengers, all reportedly from Bengaluru. Their identities are as follows:Captain HimanshuSpeaking to PTI in Dehradun, Prateek Jain, CEO of the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA), said "the helicopter took off from Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1.14 pm today.As it was crossing the Joshimath Valley, we suddenly lost track of it on our tracking system, which we use to monitor its movements. We have also received some local information regarding the incident.""So far, nothing has been confirmed. However, according to the information available in the passenger manifest, a total of six people were on board the helicopter, the pilot and five passengers. The helicopter's location has not yet been traced. However, search and rescue teams have been mobilised in coordination with the Chamoli district administration," he said."The SDRF has also been deployed, along with a unit of the Army. As soon as the weather clears, we will send another rescue helicopter from here to locate the missing helicopter," Jain added.Local inputs about the incident also prompted authorities to initiate a search operation.Sub-Inspector Manohar Kanyal of Joshimath police post said information about the incident was received from the Joshimath sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) at 2.21 pm."At 14:21 hrs, information was received from the SDM Joshimath regarding the crash landing of a helicopter above Chai village in the Joshimath area," Kanyal told ANI."In this regard, UCADA officials stated that the location of a Trans Bharat helicopter, which was flying from Badrinath to Sahastradhara, is showing near the Army Camp above Chai village. Complete details regarding the crash or crash landing are not yet available," he added.Speaking to ANI, Jain said the helicopter belonged to Trans Bharat Aviation and confirmed that the company’s entire fleet had been grounded as a precautionary measure."A helicopter belonging to Trans Bharat Aviation departed from Badrinath for the Sahastradhara heliport at 1:14 PM. We have been unable to trace the helicopter's location since it was passing through the vicinity of the Joshimath valley. Upon receiving this information, we mobilised the Chamoli district administration, the SDRF (State Disaster Response Force), and an Army unit to the area near the incident site to prepare for a proper rescue operation," he said."As a precautionary measure, the entire fleet of helicopters belonging to Trans Bharat Aviation has been grounded...According to initial information, there were 6 people on board—the pilot plus 5 others. We will share further details once we have confirmation..." he added.The grounding is a precautionary step as authorities work to establish the circumstances surrounding the crash.Uttarakhand disaster management officials in Chamoli district said teams had rushed to the area to conduct search and rescue operations. Police, SDRF, Army and ITBP personnel were dispatched to the reported crash site.The location of the helicopter and the condition of the people on board remained unclear in the initial hours after the incident. Authorities were coordinating with the district administration and other agencies to locate the aircraft and assess the situation.It was also not immediately confirmed whether the helicopter was returning after ferrying pilgrims from the Badrinath shrine.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said he was closely monitoring the situation and that a joint rescue operation was under way.In a post on X, Dhami said, "Reports have been received regarding an unfortunate helicopter crash near Chai village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, the Disaster Management Department, and the SDRF.""I am personally monitoring the situation closely. I have issued instructions to ensure that those who are critically injured are immediately airlifted to a higher-level medical facility for better treatment. I pray to God for the safety of the passengers," Dhami added.The state government said the rescue operation was being coordinated by the district administration and disaster management authorities.The crash took place amid adverse weather conditions in Uttarakhand, with rainfall and snowfall reported in several parts of the state.Television channels reported that fire and smoke were visible at the crash site and that rescue teams had reached the area. Bad weather was suspected to have contributed to the incident, though the cause had not been officially established.Kedarnath Dham witnessed the season's first heavy snowfall following continuous snowfall since Thursday, October 29. The surrounding hills were covered in snow, while temperatures in the region dropped significantly.The India Meteorological Department's Dehradun centre also forecast continued rainfall over the next few days, particularly in the hill districts.Dr CS Tomar, director of the Meteorological Centre in Dehradun, said heavy rainfall had been recorded at eight to nine places across Uttarakhand on October 29, particularly in Uttarkashi, Tehri and Haridwar districts.Tomar said similar weather conditions were expected on Friday, with a higher likelihood of rainfall in the Kumaon region."Tomorrow, on the 31st, chances of light to very light rain will persist, especially in the hilly districts. Similarly, on the 1st and 2nd (of November), light to very light rain may be witnessed at isolated places, particularly in our northern hilly districts," he said.In view of the forecast, district administrations have been placed on alert to ensure the safety of pilgrims, residents and commuters.Earlier on Thursday, District Magistrate Prashant Arya directed officials to activate the District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC) in alert mode to monitor weather conditions and oversee precautionary measures.Authorities are also monitoring road conditions and the Gangotri and Yamunotri shrines through live CCTV cameras.The administration has appealed to devotees and pilgrims to take precautions against the cold and follow advisories issued by the administration and police.
Article Summary: The helicopter took off from Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1.14 pm today. Authorities lost track of it while it was crossing the Joshimath Valley and it was subsequently reported missing near Hathi Parvat. Search and rescue teams, including personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the Army, police and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), were deployed to the area following reports of the crash.

NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu has assured residents that the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) will not be imposed on them, saying the government is currently seeking cooperation only to complete its Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR).Speaking to reporters, Khandu said he was inviting the youth wing of Adi Bane Kebang (ABK) and the Adi Students' Union (AdiSU) for discussions following their recent media briefings on the project."I want to reach out to all the associations and units in the Siang area to try and provide more clarity about this project. Right now, we aren't even talking about building the dam. Right now, only the PFR needs to happen," he said.Khandu said a decision on whether to proceed with the dam would be taken only after the PFR establishes its feasibility. Even if the project is found viable, the government would consult residents in accordance with legal provisions, he added."This project won't move forward without talking to the public," Khandu said, adding that he was encouraged by the response from local organisations during his recent interactions.He said he would continue visiting the Siang region until the PFR process was completed.The chief minister also alleged that residents, particularly in Siang and Upper Siang districts, were being fed misinformation about the project. He said the government wanted to address their concerns through direct engagement.The proposed 11,200-megawatt project is planned on the Siang river and is being pursued by the Centre through NHPC. Envisaged as a multipurpose storage project, it is expected to combine hydropower generation with water management and strategic objectives.However, sections of the indigenous Adi community have consistently opposed the project, citing concerns over the possible submergence of villages, displacement, loss of ancestral land and livelihoods, and environmental damage. The project's location in a seismically active region has also raised questions about dam safety.Protests intensified in October, with demonstrations turning violent in late September and again on October 23. Protesters set fire to an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, while several vehicles and properties linked to political leaders were damaged.The unrest has prompted additional security deployment and renewed efforts by the state government to initiate dialogue. The Arunachal Indigenous Tribes Forum has also proposed setting up a peace committee to facilitate discussions between the government and groups opposing the project.Khandu's latest outreach comes amid continuing demands from local organisations for meaningful consultations and a halt to survey activities until their concerns are addressed.Tensions have persisted over the past week. On October 25, Khandu held separate meetings with legislators and indigenous community representatives to discuss the PFR, environmental concerns and national security implications. On October 29, a solidarity rally in Itanagar demanded the release of detained protesters and the withdrawal of cases.The Arunachal Indigenous Tribes Forum has since proposed a peace committee to facilitate dialogue.India's biggest proposed hydropower project, spread across three districts of Arunachal Pradesh's Siang valley, is being positioned as a strategic counter to China's mega dam planned upstream.However, the project has faced resistance from indigenous communities, particularly members of the Adi tribe, who fear that the reservoir could submerge villages and disrupt their deep-rooted ties with the Siang river.

NEW DELHI: The Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) on Saturday expelled former party general secretary Kripa Alva for six years over her alleged involvement in a sting operation targeting Congress leaders in the state. The expulsion takes immediate effect, according to an order issued by KPCC vice-president M Narayanaswamy.The order said the controversy had caused embarrassment to the party because of negative publicity and media reactions. It also cited alleged anti-party activities as the reason for the disciplinary action."As your name has figured in this sting operation case and your conduct in the matter amounts to anti-party activities, on the instructions of the Hon'ble KPCC President, you are hereby expelled from the party for a period of six years with immediate effect," the order stated.According to the KPCC, a show-cause notice had previously been issued to Alva seeking her explanation over the allegations. However, the party said she had not submitted any response so far.The action comes amid an ongoing police investigation into a video allegedly targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah.Siddaramaiah had named her behind the 'defamatory video'. The Bengaluru police said on Thursday that the sexual abuse allegation featured in the video was part of a "fabricated and deliberately constructed narrative"."The evidence gathered so far prima facie indicates that the allegations of sexual abuse portrayed in the video are part of a fabricated and deliberately constructed narrative," the police said in a statement.The police further said that statements recorded from individuals appearing in the video and the evidence collected so far did not substantiate the allegations."Their statements and the evidence collected so far, prima facie, with regard to the allegations made or implied in the recording about any individuals mentioned in the video, is false and concocted," the statement said.Investigators said the original mobile phone allegedly used to record the video had been traced, recovered and seized. It has been sent for forensic examination, with the report awaited.According to the police, the video was allegedly recorded in 2023 and purportedly concerned an incident dating back to 2011. Investigators are examining whether the recording was staged, fabricated or manipulated and are tracing its circulation before it appeared on social media in September-October 2026.The police also said the video was uploaded through anonymous accounts using VPNs, masked IP addresses and spoofed phone numbers. A mobile phone allegedly linked to the YouTube upload was traced to a shop dealing in used and refurbished devices in Delhi.One person connected with the procurement of the device was arrested from the National Capital Region on October 24. Police said preliminary findings suggested that he worked as a freelance social media content creator and may have links with politically connected individuals in New Delhi. These associations are being investigated.Alva had earlier appeared before the Central Crime Branch (CCB) on October 26, where she was questioned and her statement recorded. Police sources quoted by news agency ANI said she had also been questioned on previous occasions.Siddaramaiah had named Alva in connection with the alleged sting operation and obtained a court injunction restraining media organisations from airing or publishing the video. His son and minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah had also alleged the involvement of some Congress leaders.The investigation remains ongoing, with police examining the video's creation, ownership, circulation and the identities and possible motives of those involved.

The day is observed across the country as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas National Unity Day ), commemorating Patel's contribution to India's national integration after Independence.Patel had played a pivotal role in bringing hundreds of princely states into the Indian Union.In a post on X, the Prime Minister described Patel as the "architect of Akhand Bharat and the Iron Man of the nation", highlighting his contribution to building a strong and united India."On the occasion of his birth anniversary, heartfelt salutations to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the architect of Akhand Bharat and the Iron Man of the nation. Article Title: PM Modi attends ‘Anand Math’ play ahead of Ekta Diwas celebrations in Gujarat
Article Text:
PM Modi

EKTA NAGAR, KEVADIA: Anand Math, the literary source of ‘ Vande Mataram ’, was adapted into a grand, multimedia-based play and showcased at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, here on Friday in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the eve of the Ekta Diwas, Sardar Patel’s birth anniversary.Sardar Patel’s birth anniversary on Oct 31 this year is focused on celebrating the end of armed Naxalism and 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’. The prime minister is the chief guest at the Ekta Diwas events this year, organised here with the 'Statue of Unity’ as a backdrop. The one-and-a-half hour long play ‘Anand Math’ is directed by NSD, It is based on the abiding philosophy of Anand Math: that every person of India has a responsibility of building a bright future for the country and being aware of its cultural heritage.Members of Anand Math author Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’ family sat beside the Prime minister, watching the dramatic recreation of the Bengali novel. The innovative use of digital screens to lend a cinematic edge to the sets, set the performance apart."The Chattopadhyay family is glad that Vande Mataram is being sung in full. Justice was not being done to the sentiment behind Anand Math when just two stanzas were sung," Shantanu Chatterjee, a member of the family who watched the play Anand Math, told TOI.The play, in fact, ended with the rendition of Vande Mataram in full.Ekta Nagar, which houses the towering statue of Sardar Patel and other tourist attractions, is the venue of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas Parade, which is almost on the lines of Republic Day parade in Delhi, possibly grander with several events organised alongside the parade. The town is currently glowing with festive lights, with lit up pieces of art showcasing the culture and traditions of each state. Tourists from all over the country have descended here to watch the 'Unity Day' spectacle.On Saturday, 7,000 people from 126 districts that at some point of time were affected by Left-wing extremism, will participate both as performers and spectators in the event.Around 2,000 artists drawn from the 126 districts will join the celebrations by putting up a drama performance, also directed by the National School of Drama (NSD), through which they will recount how their life and property were threatened when Naxalism was rampant in their area.In addition, around 5,000 local people from these 126 districts have been invited. They will not only be spectators for all the performances but will also, through their interactions, share the hardships they had to undergo at the hands of Maoists and how their lives have changed now.“Their participation will underline the resilience of communities that have endured conflict and highlight the role of cultural expression in strengthening national integration,” said Govind Mohan.The 2026 edition of the parade will also feature march-past by contingents of all the central armed police forces (CAPFs) and state police personnel who were in the forefront of the decisive fight against left-wing extremist violence. A short film will play on LED screens at the venue as the contingents pass in front of the Prime Minister, the chief guest, summarising the salient feature of their achievements in eliminating armed Naxalism.The Ekta Diwas parade, to be held in the evening hours this year, will also feature tableaux designed around the theme of “Vande Mataram” and constructed by the people and private entities with corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds, with no involvement of the govt. The 15 designs for the tableaux, selected through competition, are based on the implications of ‘Vande Mataram’ on nationhood and development.There will also be a cultural programme curated entirely by people from different states and communities who have made Gujarat their home. Around 5,000 artists will showcase dances and culture of their respective states through this mega-performance.
Article Summary: Anand Math, the literary source of ‘ Vande Mataram ’, was adapted into a grand, multimedia-based play and showcased at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the chief guest at the Ekta Diwas events this year, organised here with the 'Statue of Unity' as a backdrop.

Article Title: Omar Abdullah faces internal storm: Many NC MLAs upset over J&K cabinet rejig; Srinagar MP announces resignation
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah and Farukh Abdullah (File photo)

MLAs meeting

SRINAGAR: The government of chief minister Omar Abdullah is facing signs of discontent within the ruling National Conference (NC), with a number of legislators reportedly unhappy over the recent cabinet expansion and seeking greater democracy within the party and resignation of the whole cabinet.The discontent within the party has taken place at a time when the party MP from Srinagar Aga Ruhullah Mehdi is resigning from the party on November 3 leaving Srinagar parliamentary seat open. “I will resign from the National Conference and my Lok Sabha seat on November 3, 2026. The crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family. They expect the people to vote, then know their place. They take us for fools who cannot tell a broken promise from a political necessity. Ask them to honour their own manifesto, and they lecture us on how little we understand realpolitik,” Mehdi wrote on X.“We demanded the restoration of Article 370, the release of prisoners and the protection of our rights. They sought power on those promises, then treated us as fools for expecting them to deliver. We refuse to lend our name to this humiliation. There is no fixing this rot from within. The seat was won on a promise to the people,” Mehdi added.Mehdi said he would surrender the seat rather than become an accomplice to the betrayal of that promise.Mehdi would address the people on November 3, the death anniversary of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, at Behisht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam. His father was a Congress leader and prominent Shiite cleric who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000.Ruhullah Mehdi is an alumnus of Tyndale Biscoe School and holds a bachelor's degree in arts from the University of Kashmir. His political career began in 2002, when he contested and won his first Assembly election from Budgam. He retained the seat in 2008 and 2014. In 2009, he was inducted into the state Cabinet, becoming the youngest Cabinet minister. In 2015, Mehdi was nominated as the chief Spokesperson of the National Conference, the position he held for several years. However, after abrogation of Article 370 on August 5, 2019, he distanced himself from the party’s stand of maintaining silence over the situation in Jammu and Kashmir after August 5. He would urge the party to take a stand on Article 370 rather than urging the centre to restore statehood which he describes as a scaled down position.In August this year the NC president Dr Abdullah said Mehdi would not have won the parliamentary elections without the NC support. He said that if Mehdi believed Article 370 could be restored, he should fight for it, as no one had stopped him from pursuing the cause. Dr Abdullah had said the NC had not prevented Mehdi from pushing for the restoration of Article 370. Dr Abdullah had said Mehdi should resign and contest elections on his own. In response Mehdi had said that Dr Abdullah has for the first time asked anything from him and he will not disappoint him.Meanwhile, according to the sources, over a dozen party legislators met Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone, who represents the Lolab constituency, with several others joining the meeting online. They decided to seek resignation of the entire council of ministers and demand that a new cabinet be formed through consensus, based on merit and in keeping with democratic principles, sources said. They also decided to seek the resignation of the chief minister’s advisor Nasir Ahmad Wani.In a related development, NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah removed Mubarak Gul as the party’s general secretary. Gul was among the MLAs who attended the meeting at Lone’s residence. After the cabinet expansion on Tuesday, Dr Abdullah had elevated Gul, who wanted cabinet induction for himself, to the post of general secretary.Omar Abdullah and Dr. Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi.Dismissing reports of widespread discontent within the party and rebellion, NC spokesperson Ifra Jan questioned the claim that 20 MLAs attended the meeting at Lone’s residence. “They are saying 20 MLAs held this particular meeting. Where is this figure of 20 coming from? Is there a photograph or a list of names? Somebody anonymously claims 20 and everyone else repeats it without any investigative corroboration,” she said.“After the cabinet expansion, I think one or two MLAs openly expressed their displeasure and that was there for everyone to see. Isn’t that normal? Doesn’t this happen in all political parties? Some MLAs are happy while others are unhappy. This is common practice across the country,” she said.“Ever since Omar Sahib (Omar Abdullah) took oath, the leader of the opposition BJP's Sunil Sharma, has been claiming that the government will fall next week. Unfortunately, nobody is asking why. Every disagreement is being viewed through the prism of “government will fall rumours” without any evidence. We consider any claim of large-scale discontent within the party as a rumour,” she added. Sunil Sharma said it seems Omar Abdullah government has only eight MLAs with it and those eight are cabinet Ministers.Nazir Gurezi, who was part of the meeting, told the TOI that Lone had invited all MLAs and “large number of MLAs were at his residence. We just had food there”.On Tuesday morning Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha administered the oath of office and secrecy to the newly inducted ministers, Ali Mohammad Sagar, Shamima Firdous, Mir Saifullah and Altaf Ahmad Kaloo at Lok Bhawan in Srinagar taking the number to eight with Omar including nine. Omar dropped Satish Sharma, who was Minister for food, consumer affairs, transport science, IT, youth affairs, sports, and training.Omar was sworn in as chief minister on October 16, 2024, along with five ministers. Under the prescribed norms, the council of Ministers cannot exceed 10% of the total strength of the legislative assembly. With 90 members, the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly can have a maximum of nine ministers, including the chief minister. Three cabinet berths had remained vacant for nearly two years as the party struggled to decide whom to induct.Soon after the expansion on Tuesday, NC MLA Abdul Majeed Larmi broke down. “I deserved a place in the cabinet. I felt very sad not to be part of the cabinet. I was deserving of it (cabinet seat). Till the last moment, I was expecting to be part of the cabinet,” Larmi said. “I am a law graduate, while the MLA chosen has not even passed matriculation,” he had said.Mubarak Gul’s supporters lodged a protest at the party headquarters.In the 90-member Assembly, the NC has 41 MLAs and is backed by six independent legislators, while the Congress, with six MLAs, extends support to the government from outside.
Article Summary: Aga Ruhullah Mehdi is resigning from the party on November 3 leaving Srinagar parliamentary seat open. Mehdi said he would surrender the seat rather than become an accomplice to the betrayal of that promise. Over a dozen party legislators met Friday evening at the residence of Qaiser Jamshaid Lone. They decided to seek resignation of the entire council of ministers.

Article Title: 'Credibility rests on even-handedness': India flags politicisation of UNHRC
Article Text:
First secretary at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan

India calls for equal emphasis on all human rights

India raises concerns over funding and duplication of mandates

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has said the credibility of the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) depends on “even-handedness”, warning that country-specific mandates pursued without the involvement of the concerned nation deepen divisions rather than improve human rights conditions on the ground.Addressing the United Nations General Assembly's debate on the Human Rights Council's report on Friday, First Secretary at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, called for dialogue, cooperation and equal treatment of all countries in addressing human rights concerns.She said country-specific mandates pursued without the engagement of the country concerned seldom improve conditions on the ground and instead create divisions within the council.“Credibility of the council rests on even-handedness. Country-specific mandates pursued without the engagement of the country concerned seldom improve the situation on the ground,” she said.Recalling external affairs minister S Jaishankar's remarks at the high-level segment of the 61st Human Rights Council in February, Mangalanandan said human rights should be advanced through dialogue and genuine partnerships rather than selective approaches.Jaishankar had said that “human rights are best advanced through dialogue, capacity building and genuine partnerships, and not by politicisation, selectivity, or double standards.”Mangalanandan said such an approach was necessary for the council to speak with one voice and address allegations that human rights were being weaponised.She also identified the Universal Periodic Review (UPR), which involves cooperation and engagement with member states while treating all countries equally, as the appropriate platform for assessing human rights records.India also stressed that economic, social and cultural rights, along with the right to development, should receive the same attention as civil and political rights.“Economic, social, and cultural rights and the right to development deserve the same attention as civil and political rights,” Mangalanandan said.She noted that poverty, debt and limited access to financing and technology remained major obstacles to the enjoyment of human rights across much of the developing world.“These call for international cooperation and not coercion,” she said.India also flagged terrorism as one of the gravest threats to human rights, particularly the fundamental right to life, and called on the council to maintain sustained attention to the issue.“We would encourage the council to give this threat the sustained attention it warrants on the basis of zero tolerance,” she said.Mangalanandan said the Human Rights Council should fulfil its mandate within the resources available to it and called for transparent, member-driven rationalisation of its work.She cautioned against budgetary measures disproportionately affecting mandates dealing with development and economic, social and cultural rights.“Rationalisation should remain member-driven and transparent. It should not fall disproportionately on mandates that address development and economic, social, and cultural rights,” she said.India also called for adequate and predictable funding for the UN's human rights pillar through the regular budget, arguing that its priorities should not be determined by earmarked voluntary contributions.Mangalanandan further flagged duplication between resolutions and initiatives taken up by the Human Rights Council and the UN General Assembly.“We should consider mechanisms that avoid resolutions and initiatives on the same topic and of similar nature, both in the Council and (General) Assembly."We see an increasing tendency for the Council to dictate reporting to the Third Committee, including reporting by Special Rapporteurs, which further undermines the need for a specialised Council,” she said.The Third Committee of the UN General Assembly deals with social, humanitarian and cultural issues.India returned to the Human Rights Council in 2026 for its seventh term, covering the 2026-28 period.
Article Summary: Country-specific mandates pursued without the involvement of the concerned nation deepen divisions rather than improve human rights conditions on the ground. First Secretary at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, called for dialogue, cooperation and equal treatment of all countries in addressing human rights concerns.
